name: Source Definition
definition: Holds the definition of each external source: what it is, what data it delivers, and how often it delivers it. Keeps that definition through its life, from the first statement to its withdrawal.
rationale: The platform cannot acquire from a source, and cannot know that a source failed, without a statement of what the source promises. A source changes its schedule and its content. A definition that the platform cannot change becomes the cause of a report that is not true.

name: Acquisition
definition: Obtains data from a defined source. The platform asks the source on the schedule that the definition states, or the source sends the data without a request.
rationale: A source gives its data in one of two ways. The platform must accept both, because the source decides how it behaves and the user does not.

name: Normalisation
definition: Converts a delivery into the form that life state uses.
rationale: A source uses its own form and life state uses one form.

name: Delivery Assurance
definition: Compares what a source delivered against what its definition states, and reports a source that did not deliver.
rationale: A source can stop without a message. Nothing else in the platform can tell the difference between a source that has no new data and a source that failed.

name: Attribution
definition: Gives each item the source that supplied it, the time of the observation, and an identifier that stays the same across deliveries from that source.
rationale: Only the system that received the delivery knows where the data came from and when. State Custody cannot find this out later.
